newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on market concerns.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on market concerns.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed sharply down on Wednesday on concerns about concrete steps to keep domestic investors from buying B shares and caution about poor 1996 company results, brokers said.
The B index fell 1.128 points or 1.59 percent to 69.752 points on volume of 14.1 million shares worth $7.6 million, against Tuesday's $10.4 million.

Brokers said market talk that Beijing would take measures this week to force domestic investors out of B share trading dampened market sentiment, compounded by a poor performance in the A share market.
"Talks that domestic investors will be forced out of trading next week sparked the market concerns," one broker said.
China's securities authorities have several times reaffirmed the ban on domestic investors buying B shares but they have yet to translate into no effective measures, brokers said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 33 down, four flat and six up.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, plunging $0.020 or 9.09 percent to $0.200 on volume of 30,000 shares.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the most active, falling $0.010 or 1.04 percent to $0.950 on volume of 1.5 million shares on profit-taking.
Shanghai's A share index was down on a technical correction caused by concern about possible government intervention in the over-speculative market, brokers said.
The A index edged down 0.959 points or 0.08 percent to 1216.271 points on volume of 765.1 million shares worth 9.3 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 index fell 1.998 points or 0.06 percent to 3233.236 points.
Tianjin Global Magnetic Card was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping 2.30 yuan or 7.35 percent to 28.90 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
